title: Letter to Calosyrius
blurb: Cyril of Alexandria writes to Calosyrius, Bishop of Arsinoë, about monks who taught that God has a human body because man was made in the image of God. Cyril answers that God is spirit, without body or shape, and that the image lies in reason, virtue and rule over the earth. A fresh English translation from the Greek.
scope: The first part of the letter, on the image of God, ending where Cyril turns to those who say the Eucharist kept to another day no longer sanctifies. The rest of the letter (on the reserved Eucharist, monks who refuse to work, and the Melitians) is not yet translated.

text_history.method: A fresh English translation made from the Greek text printed in PG 76 (Ad Calosyrium). No published English version was used for its wording.
